finding: the unix-address creator binds credentials.sock through its held job descriptor as /proc/self/fd/<d>/credentials.sock and Linux /proc/net/unix keeps that sun_path verbatim, but _creator_status accepted only a listening row whose path equals the canonical job pathname, so listenerReady stayed false on every Linux HOST before any credential handoff

reviewedFirstFix.finding: review only: the first fix read /proc/net/unix as text, split it with splitlines() and took any one matching row, but the kernel ends a row only at a newline and prints a socket name verbatim, so a local socket name could carry a row naming a creator socket that was not its live listener

nativeEvidenceLimits: the synthetic /proc reproduces only the kernel output format; the actual bind, /proc/net/unix, verbatim names and descriptor links are qualified on Linux by CredentialWireTests and the actual-kernel listener test, and no native creator attempt has met this status yet
